discovery: Discovery of gamma-ray burst afterglows and the cosmological origin of gamma-ray bursts

nominees.name: Filippo Frontera
nominees.affiliation: University of Ferrara and INAF-OAS Bologna, Italy

motivation: For three decades gamma-ray bursts were the great unsolved mystery of astrophysics. In 1997, Costa and Frontera, leading the BeppoSAX team, detected the first X-ray afterglow (GRB 970228) and delivered rapid arcminute localisations. These made optical counterparts possible. Kulkarni's group then measured afterglow redshifts and detected the first radio afterglows, showing that the bursts are cosmological, relativistic explosions. They are the most luminous events known. This breakthrough created modern time-domain astrophysics. It led to the gamma-ray burst-supernova connection, which shows that long bursts come from the deaths of massive stars, and to bursts as probes of the first galaxies and of reionisation. It also built the rapid multi-messenger follow-up methods that made the kilonova of GW170817 possible: localise fast, follow up at many wavelengths, and turn a fleeting signal into physics. Few discoveries have so fully transformed our view of the dynamic Universe.
